chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from al-Nadr from 'Abdullah ibn Sinan said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the Adhan, so he said: 'You say - Allahu Akbar, Allahu Akbar. Ashhadu an la ilaha illa Allah, Ashhadu an la ilaha illa Allah. Ashhadu anna Muhammadan Rasul Allah, Ashhadu anna Muhammadan Rasul Allah. Hayya 'ala al-salah, Hayya 'ala al-salah. Hayya 'ala al-falah, Hayya 'ala al-falah. Hayya 'ala khayr al-'amal, Hayya 'ala khayr al-'amal. Allahu Akbar, Allahu Akbar. La ilaha illa Allah, La ilaha illa Allah.'
ai.seo_question: What are the exact words and sequence of the Shia Adhan according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* explicitly includes 'Hayya ala Khayr al-Amal' (Hurry to the best deed) as part of the Adhan, a phrase notably absent in the Sunni tradition but affirmed in Shia jurisprudence as a Sunnah. It highlights Imam al-Sadiq’s (AS) role in preserving the complete liturgical form, emphasizing the invitation to both ritual prayer and superior righteous actions. This detail underscores the Shia emphasis on the holistic nature of worship, linking the call to prayer with the broader concept of excellence in deeds.
